units.title: One mutex serialises both threads
units.summary: Mutex::push and Mutex::pop each take a std::lock_guard on the same mutex_, so producer and consumer never run queue operations concurrently.

claims.text: push and pop both lock mutex_ before touching the cursors.

units.title: Acquire/release cursors replace the lock
units.summary: Fifo3 makes each cursor a std::atomic with a single writer. The writer publishes with a release store; the other thread observes it with an acquire load.

claims.text: push stores pushCursor_ with memory_order_release after constructing the element.
pop loads pushCursor_ with memory_order_acquire before reading the element.

units.title: Cursors live on separate cache lines
units.summary: Both cursors are alignas(64) so writes by one core do not invalidate the line the other core reads.

claims.text: pushCursor_ and popCursor_ are each aligned to a 64-byte boundary.
This avoids false-sharing ping-pong between the two cores.

units.title: Fifo4 caches the other thread's cursor
units.summary: The producer keeps a private copy of popCursor_ and only reloads the shared atomic when the cached value says the queue is full.

claims.text: push reloads popCursor_ only when full(pushCursor, popCursorCached_) is true.
